extracted.intended_audience: users of GAP (computational algebraists, mathematicians and programmers using GAP for polynomial/rational-function computations)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference/manual guidance for creating, manipulating, and reasoning about indeterminates, polynomial rings, Laurent/univariate polynomials and rational functions in GAP, including attributes, operations, ordering, factorization and related utilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indeterminate naming and printing conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Indeterminates may be assigned string names for nicer printing; unnamed indeterminates are printed as "x_nr". The special printed name x_nr always denotes the variable with internal number nr. Names do not imply variable bindings; an indeterminate named "x" cannot be accessed via a program variable x unless that variable was defined to be that indeterminate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When requesting named indeterminates GAP will usually pick the first available unnamed indeterminates and name them, so no stable mapping between names and internal numbers is guaranteed. Creating an indeterminate with a name that already exists will by default return the existing indeterminate; to force a distinct new indeterminate use the :new option (generally discouraged).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indeterminate selection by number or avoidance list
rubrics_metrics.description: Indeterminate(R[, nr]) or X(R[, nr]) returns the indeterminate with internal number nr (defaults to 1); if a list avoid of indeterminates is supplied, the returned indeterminate is guaranteed different from those in avoid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may also request an indeterminate by name (Indeterminate(R, name[, avoid])). Use the avoid list to ensure fresh variables in contexts where index numbers or previously-created indeterminates should be excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: IndeterminateNumberOfLaurentPolynomial / IndeterminateNumberOfUnivariateRationalFunction
rubrics_metrics.description: Attribute returning the internal number of the indeterminate in which a univariate (Laurent) polynomial or univariate rational function is expressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A constant rational function may not have an indeterminate number; in that case this attribute defaults to 1. This affects compatibility tests for being in the same univariate polynomial ring (constants may be treated as compatible).

rubrics_metrics.name: IndeterminateOfUnivariateRationalFunction
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the indeterminate (symbol/object) in which a univariate rational function is expressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this to obtain the actual indeterminate object (not just its number) for display or further operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: IndeterminateName / SetIndeterminateName / HasIndeterminateName
rubrics_metrics.description: SetIndeterminateName(fam, nr, name) assigns a name to the nr-th indeterminate in family fam (errors if already named). IndeterminateName(fam,nr) returns the name (or fail). HasIndeterminateName tests whether a name was assigned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is a SetName convenience method to set an indeterminate's name. Using these functions you can control display names and detect whether naming has occurred; attempting to reassign an existing name raises an error.

rubrics_metrics.name: CIUnivPols (common indeterminate check)
rubrics_metrics.description: CIUnivPols(upol1, upol2) returns the common indeterminate number if both univariate polynomials are given in the same indeterminate number (or if one is constant), otherwise returns fail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this to check compatibility of two univariate polynomials for algorithms that require them to be in the same indeterminate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arithmetic operations on rational functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Rational functions form a field: addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division are supported. A quotient of two polynomials may be represented as a rational function; if you know one divides the other, use Quotient to get a polynomial quotient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multivariate GCDs are expensive and not fully implemented, so GAP does not guarantee rational functions are stored as reduced quotients; to ensure cancellation explicitly call Gcd on NumeratorOfRationalFunction and DenominatorOfRationalFunction to avoid degree explosion in some algorithms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polynomial subrings and expression domains
rubrics_metrics.description: All polynomials and univariate polynomials in the same indeterminate form subrings of the rational-function field; if two rational functions are known to be in the same subring, results will be expressed in that subring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of the ring context when combining elements so that results appear in the intended domain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equality of rational functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Two rational functions f and g are equal iff Numerator(f) * Denominator(g) equals Numerator(g) * Denominator(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This equality test is independent of common factors because GAP's monomial ordering is multiplicatively invariant; use Numerator/Denominator attributes when checking or manipulating expressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ordering of monomials, terms, polynomials and rational functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Monomials are ordered first by degree then lexicographically (with x1 > x2) using MonomialGrlexOrdering; terms compare by monomial then coefficient; polynomials compare by comparing largest terms until they differ; rational functions compare by comparing Numerator(f)*Denominator(g) with Numerator(g)*Denominator(f). For univariate polynomials this reduces to compare by total degree then lexicographically on coefficients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These ordering rules determine outputs that depend on leading terms (e.g., LeadingMonomial) and are used in algorithms that rely on admissible monomial orderings. Examples in the manual illustrate comparisons like x>y, x^2*y<x*y^2, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsPolynomialFunction / IsRationalFunction categories
rubrics_metrics.description: A rational function is an element of the quotient field of a polynomial ring over a UFD (represented as numerator/denominator). A polynomial function is an element of a polynomial ring or a rational function. GAP considers IsRationalFunction as a subcategory of IsPolynomialFunction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these category tests to dispatch algorithms appropriately; note representation differences depending on base family (UFD vs non-field).

rubrics_metrics.name: NumeratorOfRationalFunction / DenominatorOfRationalFunction
rubrics_metrics.description: Attributes returning numerator and denominator polynomials of a rational function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because no proper multivariate gcd is implemented, returned numerators and denominators are not guaranteed to be reduced; call Gcd explicitly when reduced form is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsPolynomial / AsPolynomial
rubrics_metrics.description: IsPolynomial(ratfun) is true if a rational function has denominator 1 (or constant if coefficient family is a field). AsPolynomial returns an equal rational function with denominator 1 when possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Over non-fields, quotient by a ring element may force representation as rational functions even when mathematically polynomial; use AsPolynomial to coerce when representable.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsUnivariateRationalFunction and related coefficient extraction
rubrics_metrics.description: IsUnivariateRationalFunction(ratfun) is true when numerator and denominator are polynomials in the same single indeterminate. CoefficientsOfUnivariateRationalFunction returns [ncof, dcof, val] where ncof and dcof are coefficient lists of numerator and denominator (cancelled) and val is valuation so that rfun = x^val * n/d.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use IndeterminateNumberOfUnivariateRationalFunction to find the indeterminate number. The returned numerator/denominator lists are guaranteed cancelled.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsUnivariatePolynomial / CoefficientsOfUnivariatePolynomial
rubrics_metrics.description: A univariate polynomial is a polynomial in only one indeterminate. CoefficientsOfUnivariatePolynomial(pol) returns the coefficient list in ascending order (empty list for zero).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This attribute is the canonical way to access coefficients for algorithms and conversions to/from coefficient lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsLaurentPolynomial / CoefficientsOfLaurentPolynomial
rubrics_metrics.description: A Laurent polynomial is a univariate rational function whose denominator is a monomial. CoefficientsOfLaurentPolynomial returns [cof, val] where cof is the coefficient list and val is the valuation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Laurent polynomials can be viewed as quotients of a polynomial by a power of the indeterminate; many univariate functions extend to Laurent polynomials. Use LaurentPolynomialByCoefficients for constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsConstantRationalFunction
rubrics_metrics.description: A constant rational function has numerator and denominator polynomials of degree 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for quick checks of constancy and for compatibility logic where constants may be treated as belonging to any univariate ring.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsPrimitivePolynomial (finite-field test)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a univariate polynomial pol of degree d with coefficients in finite field F_q, IsPrimitivePolynomial returns true iff (1) pol divides X^{q^d - 1} - 1 and (2) for each prime divisor p of q^d - 1, pol does not divide X^{(q^d -1)/p} - 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this to test primitivity over finite fields; false otherwise. This is relevant for constructions like primitive elements of field extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: SplittingField
rubrics_metrics.description: SplittingField(f) returns the smallest field containing the coefficients of f and all roots of f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for algebraic extensions and root-field constructions; useful when factoring or computing Galois groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructing univariate polynomials
rubrics_metrics.description: UnivariatePolynomial(ring, cofs[, ind]) constructs a univariate polynomial in ind with coefficients cofs. UnivariatePolynomialByCoefficients(fam, cofs, ind) constructs a univariate polynomial over family fam and should be used in algorithms to avoid overhead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer UnivariatePolynomialByCoefficients in performance-sensitive code to avoid overhead of the generic constructor.

rubrics_metrics.name: DegreeOfLaurentPolynomial
rubrics_metrics.description: DegreeOfLaurentPolynomial(pol) returns the largest exponent n of a monomial x^n in pol; degree of zero is defined as -infinity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to compute degrees for Laurent/univariate polynomials; consistent with examples in the manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: RootsOfPolynomial and RootsOfUPol
rubrics_metrics.description: RootsOfPolynomial([R,] p) returns all roots of univariate polynomial p over ring R (defaults to polynomial's coefficient ring). RootsOfUPol([field,] upol) returns roots in upol's default domain or in the specified field; special string "split" uses splitting field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RootsOfPolynomial may return only roots in the given domain; use appropriate field argument for algebraic extensions or splitting field computation.

rubrics_metrics.name: QuotRemLaurpols (euclidean division/internal function)
rubrics_metrics.description: QuotRemLaurpols(left, right, mode) computes euclidean division of left by right (no tests). Depending on integer mode (1..4) returns quotient, remainder, [q,r], or quotient if remainder zero else fail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internal helper for euclidean division; understand mode semantics when calling directly from algorithms.

rubrics_metrics.name: UnivariatenessTestRationalFunction
rubrics_metrics.description: UnivariatenessTestRationalFunction(f) tests whether f is univariate (or a Laurent polynomial) returning [isunivariate, indet, islaurent, cofs]. If univariate islaurent true then cofs = CoefficientsOfLaurentPolynomial; if islaurent false cofs = CoefficientsOfUnivariateRationalFunction. Otherwise entries are fail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of lack of proper multivariate gcd, functions that are reducible to univariate may still return fail in some cases; use this function to detect univariate structure before applying univariate-only algorithms.

rubrics_metrics.name: InfoPoly (info class and convenience for univariate syntax)
rubrics_metrics.description: InfoPoly is the info class for univariate polynomials. Certain functions for multivariate polynomials allow a simpler syntax for univariate polynomials dropping the need to specify the indeterminate (e.g., Value, Discriminant, Derivative, LeadingCoefficient, LeadingMonomial).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When writing interactive code with univariate polynomials you can use these shorthand forms; Info classes control message reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: DegreeIndeterminate
rubrics_metrics.description: DegreeIndeterminate(pol, ind) returns the degree of polynomial pol in the indeterminate ind (or its number).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to get partial degrees in multivariate polynomials, e.g., degrees in x vs y.

rubrics_metrics.name: PolynomialCoefficientsOfPolynomial
rubrics_metrics.description: PolynomialCoefficientsOfPolynomial(pol, ind) returns the coefficient list whose entries are polynomials not involving ind, describing pol viewed as a polynomial in ind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ind can be given as an indeterminate object or its number. Useful for separating a polynomial into coefficients in one variable.

rubrics_metrics.name: LeadingCoefficient and LeadingMonomial
rubrics_metrics.description: LeadingCoefficient(pol) returns the coefficient of the leading monomial of pol (with respect to MonomialExtGrlexLess ordering). LeadingMonomial(pol) returns the leading monomial as a list of indeterminate numbers and exponents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are primary building blocks for term-based algorithms; monomial ordering affects what is considered leading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derivative for univariate rational functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Derivative(ratfun[, ind]) returns derivative of ratfun by its indeterminate if univariate; if an ind is supplied, differentiates regarding ratfun as univariate in ind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ind can be an indeterminate or its number. Use when performing calculus-like manipulations on rational functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discriminant
rubrics_metrics.description: Discriminant(pol[, ind]) returns the discriminant of a univariate polynomial pol with respect to ind (or its number).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can be used in algebraic computations; two-argument form treats pol as univariate in the given indeterminate/number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resultant
rubrics_metrics.description: Resultant(pol1, pol2, ind) computes the resultant of pol1 and pol2 with respect to ind, treating both as univariate in ind and returning an element of the base ring (which may be a polynomial ring).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for elimination and computing common roots; resultant may lie in a polynomial ring when coefficients depend on other indeterminates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value (specialization/evaluation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Value(ratfun, indets, vals[, one]) replaces indeterminates given in indets with corresponding vals. If specialization yields a constant, returns coefficient-ring element. If denominator specializes to zero, error is raised. A second variant Value(upol, val[, one]) evaluates univariate polynomial at val.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be careful with default 'one' argument when evaluating structures like matrices: Value defaults 'one' to the coefficient ring identity, which can give surprising results (e.g., M+M0 vs M+1). For matrices in polynomials always give explicit one.

rubrics_metrics.name: MinimalPolynomial
rubrics_metrics.description: MinimalPolynomial(R, elm[, ind]) returns the monic minimal polynomial of elm over ring R, expressed in ind (defaults to 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimal polynomial is the monic polynomial of smallest degree with coefficients in R that vanishes at elm; used for algebraic element representations.

rubrics_metrics.name: CyclotomicPolynomial
rubrics_metrics.description: CyclotomicPolynomial(F, n) returns the n-th cyclotomic polynomial over ring F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convenience for cyclotomic constructions; e.g., CyclotomicPolynomial(Rationals,5) returns x^4+x^3+x^2+x+1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors (polynomial factorization)
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors([R,] poly[, opt]) returns the list of irreducible factors of poly in polynomial ring R (factors over CoefficientsRing(R)). For univariate factorization, optional record opt may contain onlydegs (allowed factor degrees) and stopdegs (stop when factor of degree in set found).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use opt.onlydegs to restrict search and opt.stopdegs to limit computation time. Factorization methods available only over finite fields, subfields of cyclotomics, and algebraic extensions as implemented in GAP chapters referred.

rubrics_metrics.name: FactorsSquarefree (internal squarefree factorization)
rubrics_metrics.description: FactorsSquarefree(pring, upol, opt) factors the squarefree, monic univariate polynomial upol in pring; upol must not have zero as a root. opt is an options record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This internal function is used by factoring algorithms. Multivariate factorization currently reduces to univariate factorization via homomorphism f(x1,x2,x3)→f(x,x^p,x^{p^2}), which can be very time intensive for larger degrees.

rubrics_metrics.name: PrimitivePolynomial (rationals → integral primitive)
rubrics_metrics.description: PrimitivePolynomial(f) on a rational-coefficient polynomial f multiplies by LCM of denominators and removes content (GCD) returning [newpol, coeff] with coeff * newpol = f where newpol has integral coefficients and content 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when working over Z or when preparing polynomials for integer-based algorithms.

rubrics_metrics.name: PolynomialModP
rubrics_metrics.description: PolynomialModP(pol, p) reduces coefficients of a rational polynomial pol modulo prime p and returns a polynomial over GF(p).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for modular algorithms and for probabilistic checks like factoring modulo primes.

rubrics_metrics.name: GaloisType
rubrics_metrics.description: GaloisType(f) returns an identifier of the permutation isomorphism type of Gal(f) (as TransitiveGroup(n,i)) for irreducible rational polynomials f; identification is performed by factoring Galois resolvents and is provided for degree up to 15, but can be infeasible in some cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires the transitive groups library; computation may be infeasible for some polynomials (especially certain degree-14 cases).

rubrics_metrics.name: ProbabilityShapes (probabilistic Galois-type heuristic)
rubrics_metrics.description: ProbabilityShapes(f) returns a list of most likely Gal(f) type(s) based on factorizations modulo a set of primes; fast but probabilistic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful as a quick heuristic when exact GaloisType computation is too expensive; requires transitive groups library.

rubrics_metrics.name: BombieriNorm and MinimizedBombieriNorm
rubrics_metrics.description: BombieriNorm(pol) computes the weighted L2 norm of pol (good measure for factor coefficients). MinimizedBombieriNorm(f) applies linear Tschirnhaus transforms x→x+i to try to minimize Bombieri norm and returns [new_polynomial, i_of_transformation].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful in factorization of polynomials over rationals to control coefficient growth and to choose favorable transformations.

rubrics_metrics.name: HenselBound and OneFactorBound
rubrics_metrics.description: HenselBound(pol[, minpol, den]) returns the Hensel bound for pol (if over algebraic extension give minpol and den). OneFactorBound(pol) returns a coefficient bound for a single factor of rational polynomial pol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in rational polynomial factorization algorithms to bound sizes of factors and guide Hensel lifting.

rubrics_metrics.name: LaurentPolynomialByCoefficients
rubrics_metrics.description: LaurentPolynomialByCoefficients(fam, cofs, val[, ind]) constructs a Laurent polynomial over coefficient family fam in ind (default 1) with coefficients cofs and valuation val.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to construct Laurent polynomials directly from coefficient lists and valuation.

rubrics_metrics.name: CoefficientsOfLaurentPolynomial
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns a pair [cof, val] for a Laurent polynomial where cof is the coefficient list (ascending) and val is the valuation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides compact representation; examples show Numerator/Denominator extraction from Laurent polynomials and multiplication producing expected coefficient arrays and valuations.

rubrics_metrics.name: IndeterminateNumberOfLaurentPolynomial synonym
rubrics_metrics.description: IndeterminateNumberOfLaurentPolynomial(pol) is a synonym for IndeterminateNumberOfUnivariateRationalFunction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convenience alias for API consistency between Laurent/univariate rational function attributes.

rubrics_metrics.name: UnivariateRationalFunctionByCoefficients
rubrics_metrics.description: UnivariateRationalFunctionByCoefficients(fam, ncof, dcof, val[, ind]) constructs a univariate rational function with numerator and denominator coefficients ncof and dcof and valuation val in ind (default 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to construct univariate rational functions from explicit coefficient lists and valuation.

rubrics_metrics.name: TaylorSeriesRationalFunction
rubrics_metrics.description: TaylorSeriesRationalFunction(ratfun, at, deg) computes the Taylor series of ratfun up to degree deg at point at.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for local expansions; example shows series expansion up to degree 11.

rubrics_metrics.name: PolynomialRing construction variants and indeterminate handling
rubrics_metrics.description: PolynomialRing(R, rank[, avoid]) creates a polynomial ring over R in rank indeterminates (index numbers 1..rank). PolynomialRing(R, names[, avoid]) uses list of names to label indeterminates (new internal numbers). PolynomialRing(R, indets) uses a list of existing indeterminate objects. PolynomialRing(R, indetnums) uses index numbers. When avoid is given its indeterminates are skipped.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To get indeterminates use IndeterminatesOfPolynomialRing. Indeterminates created independently via Indeterminate normally differ though they may display identically if named. Two approaches: create ring then IndeterminatesOfPolynomialRing, or create indeterminates then create ring from them. Shortcut: ring.i or ring.name accesses i-th indeterminate or named indeterminate; index i is an index into ring's indeterminates list, not necessarily the indeterminate internal number.

rubrics_metrics.name: IndeterminatesOfPolynomialRing and IndeterminatesOfFunctionField
rubrics_metrics.description: Attributes returning a list of indeterminates of a polynomial ring or function field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these to extract indeterminate objects for manipulation or naming; note internal numbering semantics discussed in PolynomialRing guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: CoefficientsRing
rubrics_metrics.description: CoefficientsRing(pring) returns the base ring R over which polynomial ring pring was defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to inspect or verify the coefficient domain of a polynomial ring; important for domain-sensitive operations (factorization, reductions).

rubrics_metrics.name: IsPolynomialRing and specialized polynomial-ring categories
rubrics_metrics.description: IsPolynomialRing(pring) tests whether pring is a polynomial ring. Specialized categories include IsFiniteFieldPolynomialRing, IsAbelianNumberFieldPolynomialRing, IsRationalsPolynomialRing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category tests allow dispatching algorithms optimized for particular coefficient types (e.g., finite-field factoring methods).

rubrics_metrics.name: FunctionField creation and IsFunctionField
rubrics_metrics.description: FunctionField(R, rank[, avoid]) (and name/indets/indetnums variants) creates a function field over integral ring R with specified indeterminates. IsFunctionField(ffield) tests category membership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Function fields created similarly to polynomial rings; use IndeterminatesOfFunctionField to access indeterminates.

rubrics_metrics.name: UnivariatePolynomialRing constructor and IsUnivariatePolynomialRing
rubrics_metrics.description: UnivariatePolynomialRing(R[, nr]) or UnivariatePolynomialRing(R[, name][, avoid]) returns a univariate polynomial ring in a chosen indeterminate. IsUnivariatePolynomialRing tests whether a ring has one indeterminate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If nr not given it defaults to 1; using avoid list ensures distinct indeterminate choices. Univariate polynomial rings admit the simpler univariate syntax for many functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monomial orderings and admissibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A monomial ordering is total, invariant under multiplication and admits no infinite descending chains; typically must be admissible (compatible with products). Monomial orderings provide MonomialComparisonFunction and MonomialExtrepComparisonFun to compare monomials (return true iff left < right).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose admissible orderings for algorithms that rely on multiplicative invariance (e.g., Groebner-basis style algorithms). GAP represents monomial orderings as objects with comparison function attributes; use IsMonomialOrdering to test.

rubrics_metrics.name: LeadingMonomialOfPolynomial (uses monomial ordering)
rubrics_metrics.description: LeadingMonomialOfPolynomial returns the leading monomial according to the chosen MonomialExtGrlexLess (or other) monomial ordering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation of leading monomial depends on the monomial ordering chosen; affects LeadingCoefficient and many algorithmic outcomes.
